findings.reason: Independently reproduced at fdcd54e: check_errata.versions_checked reports the missing sourceVersions because E3 affects a stated result; collation.provenance returns published and exposure omits this paper. An in-memory copy with the actual preprint URL, recorded access date and matching SHA-256 returns no version error, provenance preprint, and one exposure row naming E3. Downloaded arXiv:2006.02356v1 reproduces SHA-256 210c746b6b69d466d19a0a90e8f00ca57bf2d4dfb1818b0a9955fe91ae061efb; pp.20-21 contain the cited statements. Add that explicit preprint record and preserve the statement that the revised Annals text was not obtained. The original 2026-09-22 date describes the extraction's recorded access; this verifier read on 2026-09-30. A publisher landing page is not evidence of reading its article. Correct the fallback separately within an authorized tooling task; this review changes neither tooling nor generated collation files. No conclusion about the published wording follows from this verification.

Read the three ST.5 nodes, their hypotheses and proof outlines, against BLS Definition 2.1 p.4, Lemma 3.11 p.12, (5.3) p.50 and (5.11) p.53. They plan the same unweighted coefficient/Veronese carrier, normalized primitive-residue count sigma(a;Q), CRT multiplicativity and prime-power minor-valuation identity. The extraction still marks the three items missing and places them in route 7, whose brief asks the pending Heights Part II design to cover these objects again. Use planned references to these exact ST.5 nodes and remove their duplicate route assignments; align owner metadata and the design brief. These are plans in a partial packet, not formalized results. Preserve consumer-specific primitive-image/norm lemmas and the other Part II results: the proposed 'only S_V and the real factor' restriction applies to these shared carriers, not to all of route 7. GN.0 remains the proposed owner for the general maximal-minor gcd and saturation API; no completed general minor-gcd node was found there, so ST.5's rank-two specialization needs an explicit supplier request/equivalence, not a fictitious existing import.

PV's author PDF, section 2 and Theorem 3.6/proof p.3, uses coefficient boxes, Hensel lifting, Lang-Weil uniform in fixed n,d and the codimension-at-least-two reducible locus. The extracted pv-density-ball asserts the required Euclidean limit without decomposing those inputs; route 4 is absent from ST.2's remaining coverage and no node supplies its three items. Add the proof route and an ST.2 node or explicit remaining/request entry. Use the existing quantitative Ekedahl sieve on the coefficient ball: for codimension two its normalized tail is O(1/(M log M)+1/A). Supplement the proposed repair with a uniform bound on the singular locus so Lang-Weil gives a smooth point, spreading out the reducible locus outside finitely many primes, finite-place/real boundary-nullness and congruence equidistribution, positivity of the product, and justified primitive-vector/sign-quotient normalization. The real factor is the ball fraction of the real-soluble cone, not the box factor. Reuse/generalize the discriminant-nullity input of null-singular instead of duplicating it; its current n>=3 range does not itself handle conics. Treat the conic zero-density case separately by box containment and comparable total counts. FF.2's uniform Lang-Weil node is only planned and explicitly has upstream proof gaps; name them as obligations rather than claiming this reference closes the proof.

Read BLS (2.9)-(2.12) pp.4-5 and the cited uses pp.44,49-52,57; read Nat.primorial_le_four_pow at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, NumberTheory/Primorial.lean:141. Its unconditional statement n# <= 4^n implies theta(w)<=w log 4. Splitting primes at sqrt(w) gives pi(w) log w <= sqrt(w) log w + 2 theta(w), hence log W <= sqrt(w) log w + 4(log 4)w <= 6w eventually. Thus W<=B^(6/log log B) suffices. The extracted log W~3w statement is faithful and is not refuted: retain it as an optional source statement with its PNT prerequisite, and separate the weaker consumed bound. Update dependent auxiliary constants coherently (including powers of W and the change from B to A); do not assert that the elementary proof establishes the printed constant 4. The downstream comparisons only need fixed constants divided by log log and remain valid for sufficiently large parameters.

Compared the extraction's route item lists with both review files and BLS pp.51-57. Route 4 has pv-density, conic-density and pv-density-ball; route 5 has sigma-first, sigma-variance, gradient-strata, gradient-count, sigma-lower and hensel-level-lift. Lemma 5.1/factor-comparison belongs to route 7, Lemma 5.4 to route 5, and sigma's carrier should now import ST.5 as in finding 2. The review JSON incorrectly assigns sigma/convergence and Lemmas 5.1-5.4 to route 4, and its route 5 explanation omits Lemma 5.4 and the Hensel input. Correct those explanations without reversing the accepted ownership decisions. The report's broad 'local-density product and its tails' wording can be made explicit; it does not itself contain all the JSON's incorrect claims. Page 51 expressly says the limiting singular factors are unused. Independently, for f=X_0^d, sigma(f;p^r)=p^(r-ceil(r/d))(1-p^(-n)), so the unrestricted finite-factor convergence must not be introduced as a prerequisite.

Read Bhargava arXiv:1402.1131v1 section 1.1 pp.2-3, Theorem 4/proof discussion p.5, Theorem 11 p.8 and the conclusion of the Theorem 2 proof p.11. Theorem 2 applies to every compact region described there, including the Euclidean ball in the ten-dimensional space of ternary cubics; the current maximum-coefficient specialization is true but unnecessarily narrow. Record the stronger source statement and the rank-one input of Bhargava-Skinner, the 3-Selmer parametrization/count and the fundamental-domain covering transfer. Reuse the existing ST.4 remaining entry for PAPER-SKINNER-20 route 6/Theorem D and the ST.1/ST.2/ST.5 Selmer planning obligations rather than creating a second owner. Correct 'source not yet acquired' when the owner incorporates this reading. Qualification: the extraction's twenty-dimensional inscribed box is not a dimension error; BLS p.3 passes from ten plane-cubic coefficients to twenty cubic-surface coefficients using a coordinate hyperplane. Keep that application argument (or replace it with an explicit product-region transfer), including primitive/sign normalization. It is not supplied merely by stating the ten-dimensional ball theorem.
